Direct verifier tested all graphs in five q,r regimes with small old-base adjacency patterns; finite tests corroborate but do not prove infinity.

originality.rationale: Compared complete statements and their implications. The original Henson and Conant results are finite-extension infrastructure. The indexed q=2 independent-base high-arity result supplies a related counting method but does not cover q>=3 and its nontrivial K_q-free limiting ensemble. The indexed maximal-clique-base spectral theorem uses different old-parameter geometry and yields different rare-event structure. Neither covers the exact three leading exponential bases with two-clique q-1 overlap for all q>=3, nor the q+1-arity closed census. Unindexed generalizations remain a historical risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialized counting paper could cover the q>=3 independent-base asymptotic even if it uses different terminology.
The method generalizes a known triangle-free independent-base product formula; historical priority for the clique-overlap hierarchy cannot be certified by negative searches.

value.rationale: A natural finite-base model-theoretic sampling invariant exhibits a sharp hierarchy of concentration: the typical internal tuple graph becomes K_q-free; one rare q-clique or two highly overlapping q-cliques dominate successive conditioned strata. The exact critical-arity three-exponential law reveals the entire spectrum and has nontrivial many-graph leading mass, unlike the earlier maximal-clique-parameter edgeless regime. This is structural and motivated, not an arbitrary small finite count.
